prompts.text: Add a rule to pricing.py: orders with 10 or more items in total get 5% off the subtotal.
Customers say an order of exactly 100.00 still pays shipping. Fix it.
Write a failing test first for a coupon code SAVE10 in cartTotal that takes 10% off before tax, then implement it.
tests/test_pricing.py::test_tags is flaky: it fails on some CI runs and passes on others. Make it reliable.
Explain what the tests in tests/test_pricing.py actually check, and whether they would catch a wrong free-shipping threshold.
The cart tests call the real tax service and fail without network. Mock it out so the tests run offline.
Use a subagent to add tests for the shipping rules in pricing.py while you check the rest of the module for problems.
My AI coding agent writes over-mocked tests that can never fail. Fix what is wrong with the tests in tests/test_pricing.py.
Add free delivery to cart.js: carts whose net total is over 50 get a delivery fee of 0 instead of 3.99.
A quantity of 0 slips through subtotal() without an error. Fix that.
Using TDD, add a member flag to total(): members never pay shipping.
test/cart.test.js fails on CI about one run in ten. Find out why and fix it.
Look at tests/test_pricing.py: which of these tests would still pass if shipping() always returned 0?
The tests for total() read the real rates.json. Give them their own rates so a change to that file can't break them.
Hand the job of writing tests for cart.js to a subagent, then summarise what it covered.
Increase test coverage for pricing.py.
Run the test suite and tell me what fails.
Add pytest-cov to the project config so coverage is reported on every run.
Rename the variable sub in total() to net_amount.
Add a JSDoc comment to every function in cart.js.
Raise the minimum Python version in pyproject.toml to 3.11.
Make the test runner run tests in parallel with pytest-xdist.
What does node --test do differently from jest? Just explain, don't change anything.
Refactor total() in pricing.py into smaller functions without changing its behaviour. Leave the tests alone.
Fix the spelling mistake in the README.
Explain how the shipping rule in pricing.py works.
Why did my Claude Code bill jump this month? I mostly use the agents in .claude/agents.
/context shows about 40k tokens in skills before I type anything. The release-checklist skill in skills/ is mine. Can you help?
My Codex custom agents in .codex/agents cost a lot per run. What can I cut?

My Claude Code subagents burn a lot of tokens. Is there a skill or plugin that can audit my subagents and make them cheaper? Audit the ones in .claude/agents and tell me what is wrong. Do not edit files.
My SKILL.md files are too long and eat my context window. Shrink skills/release-checklist/SKILL.md without losing any of its instructions.
I have Codex custom agents in .codex/agents/*.toml. Find out what is wrong with them and how to optimize them. Do not edit files.
Each Task launch costs me about 20k tokens up front. What is going on with my agents?
My skill in skills/release-checklist gets loaded a lot and it is expensive. Make it cheaper to load.
Codex keeps ignoring one of my agents in .codex/agents. Can you check them?
I hit context limits early in my sessions and I suspect my own skill in skills/. Look into it.
Are the agents in .claude/agents set up sensibly for cost? Which model should each one use?
Trim skills/release-checklist/SKILL.md, it has got bloated.
Create a new skill in skills/ that formats commit messages.
Write a new subagent in .claude/agents that reviews SQL migrations.
Explain what a Claude Code subagent is and when to use one.
Optimise the slowest function in scripts/report.py.
Add a new Codex agent in .codex/agents for writing release notes.
What is the difference between a skill and a slash command?
Register a pytest marker named slow in the project config so slow tests can be skipped with -m "not slow".
Split cart.js into two modules, one for totals and one for tax, without changing behaviour. Don't touch the tests.
Add a GitHub Actions workflow that runs the test suite on every push.
Add an npm script called test:watch that reruns the tests whenever a file changes.
Add type hints to every function in pricing.py. The existing tests must keep passing unchanged.
